headline: Former skipper Shan Masood axed as Pakistan turn to youth for Sri Lanka Tests
description: <p>Pakistan have dropped former Test captain Shan Masood as selectors turn to youth and domestic performers for the two-match ICC World Test Championship series against Sri Lanka, with Babar Azam retaining the captaincy of a revamped 14-member squad announced by the country’s cricket board on Saturday.</p> <p>Three batters — Mohammad Taha, Mohammad Suleman and Sameer Minhas — have earned maiden Test call-ups, while Ali Usman and Salman Ali Agha have also been included in the squad for the series to be played in Rawalpindi and Lahore from Nov 9 to 21.</p> <p>Shan’s

description: <p>LAHORE: A judicial magistrate on Saturday granted post-arrest bail to a man accused of assaulting a woman riding a scooty on Mozang Ring Road.</p> <p>Police had <a href="https://www.dawn.com/news/2039380">arrested</a> the suspect after CCTV footage of the incident, which took place on Thursday, sparked widespread <a rel="nofollow" href="https://images.dawn.com/news/1196052/netizens-horrified-after-onlookers-watch-man-brutally-assault-woman-in-lahore-without-intervening">public outrage</a> on social media. imageAlt: Suspect accused of assaulting female scooty rider in Lahore granted bail

headline: Man accused of thrashing petrol station worker in Lahore discharged from case as parties reach compromise
description: <p>LAHORE: A judicial magistrate on Saturday discharged a man accused of <a href="https://www.dawn.com/news/2028716">assaulting</a> a petrol pump employee after the complainant reached a compromise with him.</p> <p>The incident occurred at a Jubilee Town filling station when the suspect went there to get a refill. As the salesman asked him not to smoke on the premises, the suspect came out of his SUV and allegedly thrashed him before fleeing the scene.</p> <p>The police arrested the suspect after CCTV footage of the incident went viral on social media.
imageAlt: Man accused of thrashing petrol station worker in Lahore discharged from case as parties reach compromise

headline: Aurangzeb rules out consumption-led growth, says tariff reforms will continue
description: <p>LAHORE: Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb has ruled out pursuing liquidity-fuelled, consumption-led economic growth, saying Pakistan must prioritise sustainable, export-led expansion and continue with tariff reforms to improve the competitiveness of its industries.</p> <p>The finance minister was speaking at the Lahore University of Management Sciences (Lums) on Saturday at an event organised by the American Business Forum (ABF). ABF President Osman Khalid Waheed, former State Bank governor Raza Baqir and Habib Group Vice Chairman Salman Burni also spoke.</p> <p
imageAlt: Aurangzeb rules out consumption-led growth, says tariff reforms will continue

headline: Jordan king orders 'iron fist' response to deadly church attack
description: <p>Jordan’s King Abdullah ordered security forces on Saturday to respond with an “iron fist” as authorities searched for gunmen who <a href="https://www.dawn.com/news/2039342">opened fire</a> and killed nine people during a church funeral service.</p> <p>The assailants fired for several minutes in broad daylight at the church in Karak governorate on Friday, and also wounded 40 people in the rare attack on Jordan’s Christian minority.</p> <p>Security was stepped up at malls, foreign embassies and other locations across the country, the US embassy in Amm

description: <p>ISLAMABAD: An anti-terrorism court (ATC) on Saturday directed human rights lawyer Imaan Zainab Hazir-Mazari and her spouse, Hadi Ali Chattha, to record their statements under Section 342 (power to examine the accused) of the Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC) at the next hearing in the security breach case.</p> <p>ATC Judge Tahir Abbas Sipra, who conducted the proceedings at Adiala jail, adjourned the hearing until Oct 26 after both accused declined to record their statements during Saturday’s proceedings.</p> <p>Imaan and her husband, Hadi, are facing a <a h

description: <p>French police started firing tear gas at protesters Saturday as they stepped up security in major cities, aiming to prevent a repeat of <a href="https://www.dawn.com/news/2037973">rioting</a> a week ago, on a day of fresh nationwide demonstrations over the high cost of living.</p> <p>Police in the southeast city of Lyon fired tear gas to disperse some 150 protesters near the city centre — where demonstrations had been banned — when they briefly tried to block a road, an AFP journalist saw.</p> <p>Elsewhere, authorities and rattled shopkeepers geared

description: <p>Ras Al Khaimah authorities said on Saturday that all beaches in the emirate would be closed until further notice, a day after an offshore oil leak prompted <a href="https://www.dawn.com/news/2039278">beach closures</a> in neighbouring Umm Al Quwain and Sharjah.</p> <p>The Public Services Department announced the closures in a statement shared by Ras Al Khaimah Police General Headquarters. headline: Trump’s threat to strike Iran raises public concerns, congressional questions
description: <p>WASHINGTON: President Donald Trump has renewed his threat of military action against Iran, raising questions about public support for the war and <a href="https://www.dawn.com/news/2035790">Congress’s ability to restrain further escalation</a>.</p> <p>With <a href="https://www.dawn.com/news/2038966">midterm elections</a> approaching on November 3, polls show widespread <a href="https://www.dawn.com/news/2031648">dissatisfaction with the war</a>, particularly over rising fuel prices and the risk to American troops. headline: Pakistan denounces ‘heinous’ church attack in Jordan, reiterates condemnation of terrorism
description: <p>Pakistan has strongly condemned the “heinous terrorist attack” on a funeral procession at a church in Jordan’s Karak Governorate, reiterating its condemnation of terrorism in all its forms and manifestations.</p> <p>Gunmen<a href="https://www.dawn.com/news/2039342/jordan-church-shooting-claims-7-lives"> killed</a> at least seven people and wounded dozens at a church in southern Jordan on Friday. headline: Tropical Storm Champi nears China after battering Taiwan, Japan
description: <p>A powerful storm swept towards China on Saturday after battering Taiwan and Japan’s southernmost islands, knocking out power to thousands of households and forcing the cancellation of hundreds of flights.</p> <p>Typhoon Champi was downgraded to a tropical storm as its wind speed dropped to 102 kilometres (63 miles) per hour, according to the latest update from the Joint Typhoon Warning Centre.</p> <p>Taiwanese authorities evacuated more than 5,000 people from their homes ahead of the storm, which toppled trees, brought down power lines and triggered brief flood
imageAlt: Tropical Storm Champi nears China after battering Taiwan, Japan

description: <p>One-day International cricket has gone through changes over the years, but one of the aspects of the game that has continued to be crucial is the importance of taking wickets in the middle overs.</p> <p>In the span of the last three years, which included Pakistan’s dismal 2023 World Cup campaign in India, the national side’s bowlers have struggled to strike as often as they would have liked in the middle overs.</p> <p>Haris Rauf, who has featured for Pakistan in most of the matches through this period, is well aware of the team’s shortcomings as they look forwa

headline: Section 144 imposed in Upper, Lower South Waziristan over security concerns
description: <p>SOUTH WAZIRISTAN: The district administrations of Lower and Upper South Waziristan imposed Section 144 restrictions for Saturday, restricting movement in several areas and closing markets and major routes amid security concerns and the movement of logistical supplies for security forces.</p> <p>Lower South Waziristan Deputy Commissioner Musarrat Zaman and Upper South Waziristan Deputy Commissioner Irfan Ali issued separate notifications on Friday evening, outlining restrictions on public movement, access to designated roads and other activities in the affected areas.</p
